Gulzar Ahmad Bhat vs Union Territory Of J&K on 30 May, 2024 
Author: Sindhu Sharma
Bench: Sindhu Sharma
 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Srinagar
 Reserved on: 1
 Pronounced on: 3
 WP(Crl) No.
 CrlM No. 
 Gulzar Ahmad Bhat
 S/o Gh. Nabi Bhat, R/o Nihama, Tehsil Kakapora,
 District Pulwama,6
 through his wife-Rafiqa Akhter (38 years)
 W/o Gulzar Ahmad Bhat, R/o Nihama,
 Tehsil Kakapora, District Pulwama
 .... Petitioner/A 
 Through:- Mr. Tuba Manzoor, Advocate. 
 V/s
 1. Union Territory of J&K,
 Through Principal Secretary,
 Home Department, J&K Govt.,
 Civil Secretariat, Srinagar/Jammu
 2. District Magistrate, Pulwama 
 3. Senior Superintendent of Police, Pulwama
 4. Superintendent, Central Jail, Kotbhalwal, Jammu
 .....Res
 Through:- Mr. Zahid Qais Noor, G.A.
 Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Sindhu Sharma, Judge
 Judgment
01. This petition has been preferred against the detention order No.30/ DMP/PSA/23 dated 12.05.2023, passed by the District Magistrate, Pulwama, whereby, the detentue, namely, Gulzar Ahmad Bhat, S/o Gh. Nabi Bhat, R/o Nihama Tehsil Kakapora District Pulwama, has been detained under Section 8 of the Jammu and Kashmir Public Safety Act, 1978, with a view to prevent him from acting in any manner prejudicial to the security of the State. This order of detention has been assailed by the detenue through his wife, Rafiqa Akhter. 
Gulzar Ahmad Bhat vs Union Territory Of J&K on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115370757/
1 02. The detenue has challenged the order of detention on the grounds that: -
i. The allegations in the grounds of detention are vague and mere assertions of the Detaining Authority against which no prudent man can make an effective representation. 
ii. There is not even a single activity based on the material which could constitute the grounds of detention against the detenue. 
iii. The detenue was taken into custody by Police Station Kakapora and was bound down under Section 107 and 151 of CrPC for maintaining good behavior, and this condition has not been violated by the detenue. 
iv. The Detaining Authority without assigning any compelling reason has passed the order of detention. 
v. The material relied upon while framing the grounds of detention has not been provided to the detenue by the Detaining Authority which has prevented the detenue from making an effective representation. 
vi. The respondents have not observed the procedural safeguards as provided under Jammu and Kashmir Public Safety Act as well as Constitution of India. 
vii. The Advisory Board has not heard the detenue before conforming the order of detention. 
viii. The detenue has not been informed of his right to make an effective representation and even the execution of the order has been done by an officer of the lower rank. 
03. Counter affidavit has been filed and record has been produced by the respondents. The respondents have submitted that the detenue was detained validly and legally by virtue of detention order dated 12.05.2023 by the District Magistrate, Pulwama. All the statutory requirements and constitutional guarantees have been fulfilled and complied with by the Detaining Authority. The Detaining Authority, keeping in mind the very object of the law of preventive detention which is punitive and not preventive, has ordered the detention of the detenue. 
04. The detenue has been provided with all the material relied upon by the Detaining Authority while passing the order of detention within the statutory period prescribed. In compliance to the District Magistrate's order of detention, the warrant was executed on 13.05.2023 by Inspector Latief Shabnum of DPL Pulwama and detenue was handed over to the Assistant Superintendent Central Jail, Kot Bhalwal. 
05. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record. 
Gulzar Ahmad Bhat vs Union Territory Of J&K on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115370757/
2 06. The grounds of detention, formulated by the Detaining Authority, reveal that the detenue has become sympathizer of terrorist organization and is providing all logistical support, like food,
shelter and information to the terrorists operating in the area. The detenue is also stated to be reliable and close source of active LeT terrorist Commander at Kakapora and has been in contact with him through social media networking system and instigating youth in terrorism. It is further revealed that the detenue has also aided the terrorist activities in the Pulwama area for carrying out terrorist acts on the security forces. The detenue along with associates in a preplanned manner used to mobilize the general public for unlawful activities and hatched a conspiracy with armed terrorists and staunch overground workers to attack upon security forces deployed in the area so that the peaceful atmosphere of the area gets vitiated. The detenue also tried to provoke the youth of the area to join terrorist outfits. It is also stated that the detenue is in constant touch with the terrorists operating in the area and is facilitating their movement from one place to another through unconventional routes to prolong their sustenance. His remaining at large was not considered desirable as he may get involved in subversive activities and to revive the militancy in the area endangering the integrity of the State. It is also mentioned in the grounds of detention that activities indulged in by detenue were running heavily against him and being highly prejudicial to the security of the State and in order to prevent him from indulging in such activities, it was necessary to detain him by invoking the provisions of Public Safety Act.
07. The Constitution of India, under Article 22(5), provides for detention of a person without a formal charge and trial, and without such a person held guilty of an offence and sentenced to imprisonment by a competent court. Its aim and object are to save society from activities that are likely to deprive a large number of people of their right to life and personal liberty. It is well settled that the purpose of the preventive detention by detaining of a person is not to punish him for something he has done but to prevent him from doing a particular act which is prejudicial either to the security of the State or maintenance of the public order. 
08. In "Haradhan Saha vs. State of West Bengal", (1975) 3 SCC 198, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that there is no parallel between prosecution in a Court of law and a detention order under the Public Safety Act. One is a punitive action and the other is a preventive act. In one case, a person is punished to prove his guilt and the standard is proof beyond reasonable doubt whereas in preventive detention a man is prevented from doing something which it is necessary for reasons mentioned in the Act. The relevant part of the judgment is reproduced as under:-
"The essential concept of preventive detention is that the detention of a person is not to punish him for something he has done but to prevent him from doing it. The, basis of detention is the satisfaction of the executive of a reasonable probability of the likelihood of the detenu acting in a manner similar to his past acts and preventing him by detention from doing the same. A criminal conviction on the other hand is for an act already done which can only be possible by a trial and legal evidence. There is no parallel between prosecution in a Court of law and a detention order under the Act. One is a punitive action and the other is a preventive act. In one, case a person is punished to prove his guilt and the standard is proof beyond reasonable doubt whereas in preventive detention a man is prevented from doing something which it is Gulzar Ahmad Bhat vs Union Territory Of J&K on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115370757/
3 necessary for reasons mentioned in section 3 of the Act to prevent." 
09. In "Union of India and another vs. Dimple Happy Dhakad, AIR 2019 SC 3428, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under:
"40. ...Insofar as the contention that the courts should lean in favour of upholding the personal liberty, we are conscious that the Constitution and the Supreme Court are very zealous of upholding the personal liberty of an individual. But the liberty of an individual has to be subordinated within reasonable bounds to the good of the people. Order of detention is clearly a preventive measure and devised to afford protection to the society. When the preventive detention is aimed to protect the safety and security of the nation, balance has to be struck between liberty of an individual and the needs of the society."
10. Similarly, in "Union of India and others vs. Arvind Shergill and another, (2000) 7 SCC 601, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under:
"04. ...........Action by way of preventive detention is largely based on suspicion and the court is not an appropriate forum to investigate the question whether the circumstances of suspicion exist warranting the restraint on a person. The language of Section 3 clearly indicates that the responsibility for making a detention order rests upon the detaining authority who alone is entrusted with the duty in that regard and it will be a serious derogation from that responsibility if the court substitutes its judgment for the satisfaction of that authority on an investigation undertaken regarding sufficiency of the materials on which such satisfaction was grounded. The court can only examine the grounds disclosed by the Government in order to see whether they are relevant to the object which the legislation has in view, that is, to prevent the detenu from engaging in smuggling activity. The said satisfaction is subjective in nature and such a satisfaction, if based on relevant grounds, cannot be stated to be invalid. ..........." 
11. The scope of looking into the manner in which the subjective satisfaction is arrived at by the Detaining Authority, is limited. The Court, while examining the material, which is made basis of subjective satisfaction of the Detaining Authority, cannot act as a Court of appeal and find fault with the subjective satisfaction. This matter lies within the competence of the Detaining Authority. 
12. Perusal of the record reveals that the detenue was provided all the material consisting of 11 leaves. The warrant of detention has also been duly provided and explained to him in the language he understands. 
13. The Advisory Board, after considering the matter, was of the opinion that there was sufficient cause for detaining the detenue. Perusal of the record reveals that no representation has been made by the detenue. The grounds of detention are well founded and the Detaining Authority has arrived at its subjective satisfaction after due consideration of material placed before it. All the requirements Gulzar Ahmad Bhat vs Union Territory Of J&K on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115370757/
4 contemplated under the Act have been complied with by the Detaining Authority. 
14. The decision of the Detaining Authority cannot be substituted by the Court while scrutinizing the detention order, since preventive detention is a precautionary measure to protect the society from activities which may cause harm to their life and liberty. Preventive detention being a precautionary measure to protect the society from the activities that are likely to deprive a large number of people of their rights and protect them from damaging their life and property. 
15. In view of the aforesaid, none of the constitutional or statutory provisions available to the detenue have been violated, thus, there is no merit in this petition and the same is, accordingly,
dismissed. 
16. Detention record be returned to learned counsel for the respondents by the Registry forthwith. 
(Sindhu Sharma) Judge Srinagar:
